_doc: Classifies ~/.claude/rules/*.md for the #464 subagent-preload split (docs/ultraprompt-464-subagent-preload-reduction.md). Claude Code natively loads EVERY ~/.claude/rules/*.md into BOTH the main session AND every custom Task-tool subagent (verified in code.claude.com/docs 'What loads at startup': a subagent loads 'every level of the CLAUDE.md hierarchy ... including project rules'). That is the ~208K subagent preload that dies 'Prompt is too long' on multi-file reads. FIX: keep only SAFETY-CORE rules natively loaded (reach subagents); EXCLUDE the EXTENDED rules from native load via settings.claudeMdExcludes and LIST them in the MAIN session ONLY, as an index the model Reads from on demand, via the SessionStart hook hooks/subagent-preload-main-inject.py (SessionStart never fires for subagents; SubagentStart is a separate event). The hook once injected their full text, about 405,000 characters, but hook output over 10,000 characters reaches the model as a 2KB preview (GRIP#6446), so the claimed 'main = full stack' was never true. Net: main = safety-core natively plus an index of the extended rules; subagent = safety-core only (< 150K). CC's own docs agree: 'most rules don't need to reach the subagent itself.'
_conservative_default: None since 2026-10-01: every rule must be listed in `safety_core_explicit` or `extended`, and lib/rules_scope.validate (run by tests/test_rules_scope.py) reports any rule in neither, so a new rule cannot reach main unclassified. Where a computation meets an unlisted rule anyway, lib/rules_scope.classify treats it as extended (safety_core_default: false). That changes no rule's loading: Claude Code natively loads every rules/*.md that settings.claudeMdExcludes does not name, so an unclassified rule still reaches every session and subagent until it is classified and the settings re-synced. Before this, an unlisted rule defaulted to safety-core, which is how two rules nobody classified added 4,180 characters to the always-loaded set within two days (see _note_defaulted_moves_2026_10_01). NEVER move a mechanical-safety / code-integrity / claim-integrity rule to `extended` — that would drop a safety doctrine from subagent context (SECURITY REGRESSION, a #464 hard falsifier).
_classification_principle: SAFETY-CORE iff the rule (a) mechanically prevents a dangerous action a subagent can take (guardrail evasion, secret/PII commit, cross-org leak, untrusted-content confused-deputy, force-push, shared-repo wipe, wrong-repo gh op, rendered-artifact leak), OR (b) governs the INTEGRITY of code a subagent WRITES (no-stubs, bash-safety, commit-standards, cc-enforcement, path-portability), OR (c) governs the INTEGRITY of CLAIMS a subagent MAKES (r0-critical-thinking, verify-canonical, prove-it). Everything else — memory/continuity, output-style (a subagent runs its own system prompt so output-style does not even shape it), dispatch/loop orchestration, operational reference (channel IDs/ports/VPS), and meta-doctrines — is EXTENDED (main-only).

_main_tier_doc: KERN v2, the operator's ruling of 2026-10-18 (GRIP#6658): the main-session tier. A rule listed in main_tier leaves native loading (lib/rules_scope.exclude_globs puts it in settings.claudeMdExcludes, like an extended rule) and arrives in full in the main session through hooks/main-tier-inject.py, which settings bind on SessionStart once per chunk (--chunk 0 to --chunk 5) for every kind of start, so it is delivered again after /clear and after compaction. lib/main_tier.py packs the tier into chunks of at most 9,500 characters, under the 10,000 at which Claude Code cuts a hook's additionalContext to a 2KB preview, and cuts a rule too long for one chunk into labelled parts. No subagent receives a main-tier rule, so its readers must be only talks-to-operator and/or orchestrates, and no rule in lib/rules_scope.MUST_BE_SAFETY_CORE may be listed here: lib/rules_scope.validate refuses both, and a tier that needs more chunks than settings bind. Populated on 2026-10-18 with the five operator-facing rules no subagent needs (_note_main_tier_2026_10_18).
_command_moment_doc: KERN v2, the operator's ruling 1(a) of 2026-10-18 (GRIP#6658): a rule listed in command_moment leaves native loading (lib/rules_scope.exclude_globs puts it in settings.claudeMdExcludes) and is TAUGHT instead by hooks/teach-once-gate.py (GRIP#8530), which refuses the first matching command in each recipient context, main session or subagent, with the rule's full text as the reason, then lets the same command pass; the record is renewed after compaction. Only a rule the gate names in lib/teach_once.RULES may be listed (lib/rules_scope.validate refuses any other, and any settings file that excludes these rules without binding the gate on PreToolUse for Bash). A pinned rule may be listed here because the gate keeps its reach: it arrives at the moment it matters rather than at every start.
_note_command_moment_2026_10_18: Operator's ruling 1(a), 2026-10-18 (V>>, GRIP#6658): commit-standards.md (7,208 chars; pinned in MUST_BE_SAFETY_CORE), gh-repo-resolution.md (2,702) and gpt-on-the-subscription-never-credits.md (10,407) move to command_moment. readers._doc: KERN v2 phase 1: who each rule is for. A subagent holds the capabilities its tools give it (Bash can run commands, write code, commit and send text out; Edit and Write write code; WebFetch and WebSearch send text out; Agent and Task dispatch) and every agent makes claims; handles-personal-data comes from the task. talks-to-operator and orchestrates (GRIP's loops, merges, memory and session state) belong to the main session alone. The tags say who needs a rule, not where it is delivered today: lib/rule_routing.py compares the two, and lib/rules_scope.MUST_REACH pins the readers of the floor rules. A first pass, 2026-10-06, for review.

_note_rules_index: rules/CLAUDE.md is the rules-index table (navigation), NOT a top-level CLAUDE.md. It is extended. The exclude globs are scoped '**/rules/<name>.md' so they can NEVER match the top-level ~/.grip/CLAUDE.md or a project ./CLAUDE.md (those carry no /rules/ path segment and MUST always load).

_note_never_system_python_2026_09_20: never-system-python-for-grip.md promoted from defaulted-in to EXPLICIT safety-core, and pinned in lib/rules_scope.MUST_BE_SAFETY_CORE. It was appearing in the budget test's growth term (~2976 tok) beside four rules that ARE legitimately extended by _classification_principle, and the test's remedy text said to move the non-safety ones out -- so the list read as uniformly sheddable and nothing refused this one. _note_non_rule_excludes_2026_09_20: claudeMdExcludes legitimately carries globs that are not rules/*.md, and check_settings demanded EXACT equality with the generated rules globs, so it reported the one live example as an UNEXPECTED glob and test_settings_claude_md_excludes_in_sync had been red. The glob is real: ~/.grip-worktrees is GRIP_WORKTREE_HOME's default (skills/worktree-isolation/SKILL.md), and excluding a session worktree's own CLAUDE.md stops it loading as a second copy of the operator's memory. Deleting it to satisfy the checker would have changed memory-loading behaviour to fix a checker bug. Declared here so the drift guard still fires on anything NOT in this list -- the allowance is a named set, not a wildcard.

_note_file_moment_2026_10_18: Operator's ruling 2(a), 2026-10-18 (V>>, GRIP#6658, KERN v2 phase 2): four code rules leave the always-loaded set and load at the file moment. Each now carries paths: frontmatter, so Claude Code loads it only when a file matching one of its globs is read, written or edited. lib/rules_scope.validate accepts a pinned rule (MUST_REACH) with paths: only when `file_moment` lists it, and refuses a listed rule that carries no paths:, whose paths: names no glob (paths: [] still reads as path-scoped), or that `extended` excludes (claudeMdExcludes keeps an extended rule out even on a matching file; the last two from Codex on GRIP#8526), so the list, the classification and the files cannot drift. MUST_REACH readers are unchanged, and nothing changes in settings.json: a path-scoped rule is not excluded, Claude Code loads it on a match. The globs, each from the rule's own scope: no-stubs.md takes **/*.py and bin/**, because its detector reads Python and 111 of GRIP's Python tools sit in bin/ with no .py suffix. tests-must-be-able-to-fail.md takes tests/**, **/tests/**, **/test/**, **/__tests__/**, **/conftest.py, **/test.*, **/test_*, **/test-*, **/*_test.*, **/*-test.*, **/*.test.*, **/*.spec.*, **/*_spec.*, **/*Test.* and **/*Tests.*, because its scope is every test in every repo: this checkout holds 77 TypeScript and JavaScript tests outside tests/ and prefix-named test scripts (test.mjs, test-wa.mjs, a *-smoke-test.sh), and Go, Java, Kotlin, Swift and RSpec name tests foo_test.go, FooTest.java, FooTests.swift, src/test/ and foo_spec.rb (Codex on GRIP#8526). declared-input-must-reach-the-actor.md takes lib/**/*.py, bin/**, scripts/**/*.py and hooks/**/*.py, the four directories its scope names, with bin/ whole because its Python tools carry no suffix. path-portability.md takes every code and config type, not prose: .py, .sh, .bash, .zsh, .ps1, .js, .mjs, .cjs, .jsx, .ts, .tsx, .swift, .kt, .kts, .gradle, .java, .go, .rs, .rb and .tf sources and .json, .yaml, .yml, .toml, .plist, .template, .service and .timer config, each as **/*.<suffix>, plus bin/** and scripts/** whole because their executables carry no suffix. Its ban on hardcoded user paths does not depend on the language (Codex on GRIP#8526), config is where such a path turns up in practice (17 tracked config files hold a /Users/ or /home/ literal today), and .ps1 is there because the rule names C:/Users/ and the Windows installers are PowerShell. A new code or config type has to be added to the list. path-portability.md is not pinned, so validate() would accept its frontmatter unlisted; it is listed so its frontmatter cannot be dropped, nor the rule moved to `extended`, unseen. The cost the ruling accepts: the vendor probes of 2026-10-06 (docs/measurements/2026-10-06-kern-v2-vendor-probes.md, file-write and file-edit; one run each, Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Code 2.1.289) found that the FIRST write of a new matching file, and the first edit of a matching file, ignore a path-scoped rule: it loads at that write, and the model then corrected the file. The ruling accepts that for these four code rules. visual-artifact-leak-prevention.md stays native, because for it one leaking write is the harm. bin/grip-lexicon measure on main at 8796aa9f7: 37 always-loaded files and 300,262 characters; with this change 33 files and 274,517, the four rules' 25,745. lib/rule_routing.py: 7 file-channel rules, up from 3.

ratchet._doc: Ceilings that only come down (KERN v2, P0; the operator's ruling 2026-10-06, HITL lock 3, decision 3: growth is a report plus a ratchet, never a block). bin/grip-lexicon measure reports each figure against its ratchet on every pull request (the Forward Anchors job summary), with a GitHub warning when a figure is over it and never a failure. After a change that saves characters, run bin/grip-lexicon ratchet: it lowers each ratchet to today's figure and never raises one. Raising one is a deliberate hand edit, with its reason in the pull request. always_loaded_chars is what Claude Code adds up at startup: both CLAUDE.md files and every natively loaded rule, in UTF-16 code units. It warns above 150,000 on a 1M-context session. 289,970 is main at 54b72c7c9, the day this ratchet was set. The value below is always the current ratchet: bin/grip-lexicon ratchet lowers it with each saving (first to 274,517 on 2026-10-18 when four code rules moved to the file moment, _note_file_moment_2026_10_18, then by each annex and tier pull request), and the pull request that lowered it says why; this sentence never names the figure, so it cannot go stale again (AGORA on GRIP#8553).
